title: The electromagnetic spectrum
caption: The bands run from radio (λ > 1 m) to gamma rays (λ < 0.01 nm), all the same kind of wave. Photon energy E = hf = hc/λ with hc ≈ 1240 eV nm: green light (520 nm) carries 2.4 eV, a 254 nm ultraviolet photon 4.9 eV and the 50 kV X-ray limit (0.025 nm) 50 keV.
alt: A logarithmic wavelength scale from 10^-13 m to 10^4 m with the bands radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays in order, and an FM signal, a microwave oven, a person's thermal glow, green light, a 254 nm ultraviolet lamp and an X-ray tube limit marked.
description: A horizontal logarithmic scale of wavelength in metres, long wavelengths (radio) on the right and short (gamma rays) on the left.
Bands from the lesson: radio λ > 1 m; microwaves 1 mm–1 m; infrared 700 nm–1 mm; visible 400–700 nm; ultraviolet 10–400 nm; X-rays 0.01–10 nm; gamma rays below 0.01 nm.
Markers: FM radio 3 m, microwave oven 12 cm, a person's thermal peak 9.4 μm, green light 520 nm (2.4 eV), a 254 nm UV lamp (4.9 eV), and the 0.025 nm limit of a 50 kV tube.
Higher frequency and photon energy lie to the left; the bands meet with no gaps.
